LESSON: VISUAL DISCRIMINATION

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.4: Visual discrimination

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Visual discrimination. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Match and pair pictures and puzzles among other visual objects at home and at school. discrimination activities

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: VISUAL DISCRIMINATION
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Visual discrimination helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: VISUAL DISCRIMINATION
Study Visual discrimination like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Match and pair pictures and puzzles among other visual objects at home and at school. discrimination activities

What this means
In this part you learn to Match and pair pictures and puzzles among other visual objects at home and at school. discrimination activities. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Match and pair pictures and puzzles among other visual objects at home and at school. discrimination activities.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Visual discrimination”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Match and pair pictures and puzzles among other visual objects at home and at school. discrimination activities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Visual discrimination is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Visual discrimination”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Match and pair pictures and puzzles among other visual objects at home and at school. discrimination activities)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Visual discrimination to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Match and pair pictures and puzzles among other visual objects at home and at school. discrimination activities.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Visual discrimination from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Visual discrimination: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Visual discrimination?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Visual discrimination means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Match and pair pictures and puzzles among other visual objects at home and at school. discrimination activities.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
